title: Geometric open comparison for a fixed factor-normalized coefficient model
statement: Fix ell and k as in [def-pur-condensed-open-counit-comparisons]. Given a fixed C : Models ell k satisfying FactorNormalized, and an open immersion j:U→Y over k between separated finite-type k-schemes, there is h : Preserves ell k U Y j such that the prescribed integralIdentification and extensionComparison are invertible for every integral M on U, and CounitNormalized ell k C U Y j h holds. In particular this is the geometric part of the parent argument for fixed coefficient data; no coefficient family or normalized scalar units are constructed here.

source.place: Agent-formulated open-adjunction normalization needed in Steps 2–3, using the completed reconstruction and condensed scalar comparisons; not claimed to be a literal theorem of the blueprint.

proof.text: Finite type gives Noetherianity and finite dimension, and the open immersion is quasi-compact. The two different primes make ell invertible. Integral compact-support preservation for (j,id) gives extension preservation. The ordinary/completed immersion pullback comparison and completed-pullback realization theorem give restriction preservation with the required uniform bounds and etale-origin witnesses. Restrict the actual integral open adjunction.

Write q for the normalized compact-support factorization isomorphism and t=d L(alpha) u for integralIdentification. Unit naturality and alpha R(q)=r give t q=d L(r) u=1; hence t=q inverse and t is invertible. Substitute FactorNormalized in extensionComparison and cancel the images of the consecutive inverse q and inverse t. Remove the proper identity unitors. The remaining map is the composite of the two open scalar comparisons, so is a natural isomorphism. The restriction comparison is already an isomorphism. Fully faithful constructible inclusions lift these actual ambient comparisons to natural isomorphisms b and s.

For a single coefficient extension, the inverse open comparison is the adjunct of the original open unit followed by scalar/restriction balancing. The open section-derived normalization identifies this with the internal adjunction. The triangle identity therefore gives F(eta) followed by s and the restriction of b equal to the target unit. Paste the two scalar-extension equations and use naturality of the second open comparison. Successive scalar associativity identifies the pasted restriction comparison with scalarRestriction; conjugating by the fixed encoding counits and scalarLattice gives exactly the displayed unit equation. The reasoning applies unchanged to the empty open and the identity open. No counit compatibility is assumed. Transpose the two proposed counit composites under the actual open Hom bijection. The inverse open comparison is the adjunct of the integral unit, so the two transposes are s by the triangle identities and naturality. Injectivity of that bijection gives the counit equation. Paste the two scalar stages, cancel the intermediate coefficients and remove precisely the identity proper factors as in removeIdentity. This proves CounitNormalized for the actual prescribed ambient morphisms.

from.place: A strictly partial lemma of the existing six-step open-counit argument.

lean.statement:
theorem condensed_open_unit_comparison (C : Models l k) (hC : FactorNormalized l k C)
    (U Y : Base k) (j : U.scheme ⟶ Y.scheme) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    [j.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] :
    ∃ h : Preserves l k U Y j,
      (∀ M : Integral l (Field.{u} l) U.scheme,
        IsIso (integralIdentification l k C U Y j h M) ∧
        IsIso (extensionComparison l k C U Y j h M)) ∧
      CounitNormalized l k C U Y j h
